sources.title: Qwen-VL official repository
sources.evidence: Reopened October 27, 2026. Describes Plus and Max as upgraded versions of the Qwen-VL model family, without a sized Plus base or parameter count. Its November 28, 2023 news entry already names Plus. The separate Qwen-VL/Qwen-VL-Chat section identifies a Qwen-7B language initializer, ViT-bigG visual encoder and cross-attention adapter; that component description is not assigned to Plus.

sources.title: Introducing Qwen-VL
sources.evidence: Reopened October 27, 2026. The January 25, 2024 overview describes enhanced Plus and Max family models, high-resolution input and visual capabilities. It discloses neither a nominal Plus size nor a named sized base, active count or architecture; the benchmark comparisons do not establish lineage.

sources.title: Qwen documentation: Key Concepts
sources.evidence: Reopened October 27, 2026. Classifies Qwen-VL Plus as proprietary, separately from open-weight Qwen-VL 7B-based and Qwen2-VL 2B/7B/72B-based models. The listed open-model sizes are not mapped to Plus.

sources.title: Qwen-VL-Plus Model Info (indexed legacy specification; live URL redirects)
sources.evidence: Search-index text dated August 26, 2026 reports the alias equivalent to qwen-vl-plus-2025-08-15, text/image/video input, text output, context 131072, input 129024, output 8192, and unsupported function calling in Beijing and Singapore. Direct opening instead redirects to the general models page. These technical details are retained as a lead, not independently verified live specifications.

sources.title: Model Studio Qwen-VL-Max and Qwen-VL-Plus update notice
sources.evidence: Reopened October 27, 2026. The September 3, 2025 notice schedules the stable qwen-vl-plus alias to move from qwen-vl-plus-2025-05-07 to qwen-vl-plus-2025-08-15 beginning September 16, 2025 in Beijing and Singapore. It identifies no sized base, total or active count. The alias history prevents carrying an earlier family member size into the later snapshot without evidence.

sources.title: DashScope API Reference
sources.evidence: The tools parameter section explicitly says it is temporarily unsupported for qwen-vl and qwen-audio series models. The document separately names Qwen3-VL, avoiding conflation with the older qwen-vl-plus identifier.

sources.title: Function calling: supported models
sources.evidence: The current multimodal support list names Qwen3-VL-Plus and Qwen3-VL-Flash, not legacy Qwen-VL-Plus; corroborates the direct API exclusion.

sources.title: Models.dev Qwen-VL Plus catalog record
sources.evidence: The baseline source repeats January 25, 2024, 131072 context and tools=true, and lists August 15, 2025 as last_updated. Used only to trace claims, not as primary technical verification.

sources.title: Image and video understanding
sources.evidence: The current thinking-mode documentation lists newer Qwen3-VL and other newer series. It does not give an exact legacy qwen-vl-plus thinking-mode declaration; omission is not treated as sufficient proof of false.

sources.title: Attempted Qwen-VL-Plus 2025-08-15 snapshot specification
sources.evidence: The dated snapshot named by the official alias update notice returns an Alibaba 404 error document, despite HTTP 200. No model specification was accessible. The corresponding Chinese path and QwenCloud model path also failed to provide a snapshot card.

sources.title: Notice on decommissioning selected historical snapshot models
sources.evidence: Lists qwen-vl-plus-2025-08-15 among historical snapshots scheduled for decommissioning in Beijing and Singapore on May 13, 2026. Does not provide its context or modality specification, and does not identify the bare alias as decommissioned.

sources.title: Official Qwen-VL-Plus specification, August 26 2026
sources.evidence: Parent read the complete indexed official model card. It maps the alias to 2025-08-15, specifies 131072 context and text/image/video input with text output. This is last documented specification evidence; direct fetch timed out and current API operation was not tested.

sources.title: Qwen-VL-Plus official model card, fresh indexed retrieval
sources.evidence: Read the complete indexed card on October 27, 2026; direct rendering exceeded the 4 MiB tool limit. It maps qwen-vl-plus to qwen-vl-plus-2025-08-15 and gives capability, context, pricing and rate-limit tables. It provides no nominal parameter count, active count or named sized base. The previous alibabacloud.com card URL now redirects to the general models page.

sources.title: Application Feature Updates: March 18, 2025 Plus snapshot
sources.evidence: Directly reopened and read on October 27, 2026. The March 18, 2025 entry explicitly places qwen-vl-plus-2025-01-25 (qwen-vl-plus-0125) in the Qwen2.5-VL series, with 128K context and improved image/video understanding. This is family-level lineage, not a relationship to a specific sized Qwen2.5-VL model.

sources.title: Qwen2-VL: To See the World More Clearly, August 29, 2024
sources.evidence: Directly read on October 27, 2026. Announces 2B/7B open models and a 72B API. The API instructions explicitly select qwen-vl-max-0809 to access Qwen2-VL-72B. This supports that dated Max relationship, not Plus; the article gives no Plus API mapping. It also describes dynamic-resolution visual processing and multimodal rotary embeddings, so the original Qwen-VL component counts cannot simply carry across generations.

sources.title: Qwen2.5-VL launch, January 28, 2025
sources.evidence: Directly read on October 27, 2026. Releases base/instruct models in 3B, 7B and 72B sizes, without mapping Plus to any one of them. Describes structural vision-encoder changes including window attention, RMSNorm and SwiGLU, as well as dynamic frame sampling. The family release does not establish a Plus size or unchanged components from an earlier generation.

sources.title: Image Parsing Node: Qwen-VL model selection
sources.evidence: Reopened on October 27, 2026. The indexed model-selection table calls qwen-vl-plus a faster variant in the Qwen2.5-VL series and qwen-vl-max the highest-performing model in that series. Neither description identifies a sized base or count; speed, cost and benchmark positioning cannot select a parameter scale.

sources.title: LLM Reference Qwen-VL-Plus entry: unsupported 72B lead
sources.evidence: Fresh search-index retrieval lists 72B, fine-tuned and open weights, but supplies no developer statement linking Plus to a 72B base in the retrieved material. Its open-weights label conflicts with Qwen documentation. Used only to trace the previously noted 72B claim; it is not accepted as parameter evidence.

sources.title: Qwen-VL original November 28, 2023 public-availability news (December 12 README revision)
sources.evidence: The official README news item dated 2023.11.28 names Qwen-VL-Plus, describes its DocVQA performance and explicitly directs users to access the new model through the multimodal tab of the Qianwen website. This original preserved wording is stronger than the current truncated benchmark entry.

sources.title: Original Qwen-VL README commit metadata
sources.evidence: The repository API dates this immutable README revision to December 12, 2023. That commit timestamp is the preservation date; the release date is the explicit November 28 author-dated news item inside it.

name.note: Baseline display name is a harmless formatting variant of official Qwen-VL-Plus.

developer.note: Qwen Team belongs to Alibaba Group; Alibaba Cloud publishes and serves this model.

family.note: Qwen-VL is a multimodal subfamily of Qwen; existing broad family label is supported.

release_date.note: The original repository news entry dated November 28, 2023 explicitly directs users to try the new Qwen-VL-Plus model in the public multimodal web interface. An immutable December 12 revision preserves this availability sentence, which the current README later removed. This supports the public release date beyond the benchmark-only wording seen in the prior audit; January 25, 2024 is a later overview.

open_weights.note: Official documentation explicitly classifies Qwen-VL Plus as proprietary.

license.note: No open-weight model license applies to this proprietary hosted model. API service terms are separate; do not inherit the repository license.

parameters_b.note: Fresh launch, snapshot and model-card review found no developer-published nominal Plus count or explicit relationship to a named sized base. The 2025-01-25 snapshot is explicitly in Qwen2.5-VL, but no size is selected. The Qwen2-VL-72B API relationship names qwen-vl-max-0809, not Plus. Neither original Qwen-VL component sizes nor the unattributed third-party 72B label establish a Plus total.

active_parameters_b.note: No Plus-specific active count, expert-routing rule or dense activation convention is published in the freshly checked sources. Total size is also unresolved; the active count cannot be inferred from unrelated open models or family membership.

architecture.note: The explicit Qwen2.5-VL family relationship does not identify a specific Plus topology or establish dense versus MoE. Successive visual architectures change the encoder and processing design; no documented sized-base relationship supports transferring a component decomposition to the 2025-08-15 Plus snapshot.

context_window.note: Last documented exact alias specification in the complete indexed primary card; not a current endpoint availability test.

modalities.note: Complete indexed primary card confirms all three input modalities for the documented 2025-08-15 alias mapping.

reasoning.note: Visual reasoning capability in the announcement does not establish a dedicated thinking mode. No exact legacy Plus declaration was accessible to independently confirm the catalog boolean false.

tool_call.note: Direct API documentation excludes qwen-vl series from tools support; the current support list separately names Qwen3-VL. Correct the catalog true for legacy qwen-vl-plus.

description.value: Proprietary Qwen vision-language model for high-resolution image understanding, text recognition, and visual question answering.
description.note: Uses capabilities directly supported by the model-specific announcement and proprietary classification.

patch.description: Proprietary Qwen vision-language model for high-resolution image understanding, text recognition, and visual question answering.
patch.notes: Qwen-VL-Plus was publicly available on November 28, 2023 according to the original dated repository news, which linked its web interface. This is the original model release, distinct from later alias revisions. The last indexed official card maps the alias to 2025-08-15 and reports 131072 context with video input. Parameter counts and architecture remain undisclosed: the Qwen2.5-VL family relationship identifies no sized base model. Dedicated thinking mode remains unverified; endpoint availability was not tested.

summary: Fresh October 27 parameter re-audit retains undisclosed total and active counts. Official sources establish Plus family membership and the 2025-08-15 alias snapshot, but no nominal size or named sized-base relationship. The dated 72B API mapping is for Max, not Plus; original Qwen-VL components and third-party 72B claims do not transfer. Architecture remains undisclosed. A fresh release-date audit found the original November 28, 2023 repository news explicitly offering public web access, restoring that day as the release date. Thinking-mode, tools, context and modality assessments are preserved.

searches: QwenLM/Qwen-VL README commit history through December 2023

accessed_originals.evidence: The official README news item dated 2023.11.28 names Qwen-VL-Plus, describes its DocVQA performance and explicitly directs users to access the new model through the multimodal tab of the Qianwen website. This original preserved wording is stronger than the current truncated benchmark entry.

The repository API dates this immutable README revision to December 12, 2023. That commit timestamp is the preservation date; the release date is the explicit November 28 author-dated news item inside it.

findings: Current README loses the public-access sentence retained in the December 12 original revision.
The author-dated November 28 news entry describes a usable model, not only a benchmark submission.
limitations: The entry establishes public web availability, not a separate date for every API region. Later snapshot dates must not replace the original release.
